text:
Treat each user’s HR@10 as a paired binary outcome on identical candidates. For category c, record wins b_c (new hits, baseline misses), losses l_c, both-hit and both-miss counts; Δ_c=(b_c−l_c)/200, macro Δ=¼ΣΔ_c. Report percentage-point differences and 95% intervals from a paired bootstrap resampling users within each category while preserving model pairing. Exact McNemar tests assess discordant outcomes; matched-proportion intervals provide another option ([Fay and Lumbard](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9447366/)). These quantify user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates, not training-seed variability. Sampled rankings can reverse full-catalog comparisons, so retain the evaluator and describe results explicitly as HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Adaptive trial and checkpoint selection can overfit validation; an ordinary bootstrap interval around the selected winner does not correct this bias ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). For this benchmark, predeclare a maximum trial count, per-trial GPU-time cap, evaluation cadence, epoch limit, patience, macro-HR checkpoint rule and deterministic tie-break. Count checkpoint inspections as selection opportunities. Enforce 43,200 aggregate GPU-seconds across four concurrent slots, including diagnostics, debugging and failures; report actual consumption and all attempted trials. Keep preprocessing seed 0 and training/evaluation seed 42; report the 200-epoch environment default and any overrides.

Publish baseline/selected HR@10, paired counts and differences for all four categories plus the equal-weight macro score; one net hit changes category HR by 0.5 points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Retain per-user outcomes across inspected checkpoints for selection-stability analysis, labeling it exploratory rather than selection-corrected confirmation. Disclose search-space adaptations and failed/pruned trials. Reserve confirmatory claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation; never inspect test labels during search.
